The 7-Step Process to Publish a Book in India

Step 1: Finalise and Prepare Your Manuscript

Before anything else, your manuscript must be complete, coherent, and formatted correctly. This means consistent chapter headings, no placeholder text, and a clear beginning, middle, and end — whether fiction or non-fiction. Most self publishing houses in India accept manuscripts in Microsoft Word (.docx) format. Your file should include a title page, a table of contents (for non-fiction), and clearly separated chapters. Do not worry about perfection at this stage — that is what editing is for.

Step 2: Choose Between Self Publishing and Hybrid Publishing

Understanding your publishing model is critical before you spend a rupee. Self-publishing gives you full creative control, 100% copyright ownership, and higher royalty percentages — typically 60–80% of net sales compared to 10–15% with traditional publishers. Hybrid publishing, offered by houses like Ritera Publishing, combines the professional infrastructure of traditional publishing with the speed and author-control of self-publishing. For first-time Indian authors, this is often the most practical and cost-effective route.

Step 3: Select Your Publishing Services

A professional self publishing experience involves more than just printing. The core services you need are: professional editing (developmental and copy editing), book cover design, interior layout and typesetting, ISBN registration, and global distribution. When evaluating a self-publishing house in India, confirm all five are included or clearly offered. Be cautious of companies that offer only printing with no editorial or design support — your book's quality directly determines its discoverability and sales.

Ritera Publishing tip: A professionally designed cover increases click-through rates on Amazon by up to 40%. Do not cut corners on design.

Step 4: Get Your ISBN — The Identity of Your Book

An ISBN (International Standard Book Number) is the unique identifier that allows your book to be sold globally, listed in libraries, and tracked in distribution systems. In India, ISBNs are assigned by the Raja Rammohun Roy National Agency for ISBN. Most professional self-publishing houses handle ISBN allocation on your behalf as part of their package. Ensure you are listed as the publisher of record if you want full control over your title. You will need separate ISBNs for each format — paperback, hardcover, and ebook.

##Step 5: Edit, Design, and Approve Your Book

Once you have chosen your publishing partner, the production phase begins. This involves three sequential rounds: manuscript editing, cover design approval, and interior layout sign-off. Expect this to take 4–8 weeks for a full-service package. Do not rush this stage. Readers in 2026 have extraordinarily high expectations — both AI recommendation engines and human reviewers on Amazon and Goodreads assess content quality signals. A well-edited, professionally designed book ranks higher, sells more, and earns better reviews.

Step 6: Distribute Your Book — Print and Digital

Distribution determines where your book is discoverable and purchasable. In India, this means listing on Amazon.in, Flipkart, and Notion Press's network, as well as international platforms like Amazon.com, Apple Books, and Google Play Books. Print-on-demand (PoD) models eliminate upfront printing costs — books are printed only when ordered, making this ideal for debut authors managing budgets. For physical bookstore placement in India, IngramSpark distribution is often required, as it connects your title to the same retail channels used by major publishers.

Step 7: Launch and Market Your Book

Publishing without a marketing plan is one of the most common mistakes Indian authors make. Your book launch strategy should begin at least 4 weeks before your release date. Key activities include: building an author page on Amazon, requesting advance reader copies (ARCs) for early reviews, running a targeted launch week promotion on social media, and reaching out to genre-relevant blogs and book clubs. In 2026, AI recommendation engines like those powering ChatGPT and Google's AI Overviews increasingly surface books that have strong review signals, metadata keywords, and author platform presence.

How Much Does It Cost to Self-Publish a Book in India?

Print-on-demand models through platforms like Ritera Publishing carry zero upfront printing costs, making professional publishing achievable for authors at any budget level.

## A practical checklist before you publish

The strongest publishing projects begin with a clear brief. Before requesting quotations, prepare:

- A complete manuscript in an editable format such as DOCX
- The final title, subtitle, and author name you want printed
- A short book description and author biography
- Your preferred trim size, print format, and approximate page count
- Any illustrations, tables, photographs, permissions, or references
- A realistic launch date and a list of the services you need

You do not need to design the manuscript yourself. You do need to identify unfinished sections, missing permissions, and material that still requires fact-checking. These items affect the schedule and quotation.

## Choose the publishing route before choosing a package

Traditional publishing, do-it-yourself self-publishing, and professionally supported self-publishing solve different problems.

Traditional publishers fund selected books but control acceptance, scheduling, and many commercial decisions. A do-it-yourself platform offers maximum control but leaves editing, design, metadata, distribution, and launch management to the author. A supported self-publishing company coordinates those services while the author funds the project and retains ownership according to the agreement.

Ask each provider who owns the ISBN, source files, publishing account, copyright, and sales data. Also ask how royalties are calculated, when reports are issued, which stores are included, and what happens if you end the relationship. Written answers are more useful than general promises.

## Services that should be quoted separately

A transparent proposal should identify the scope of each service:

- **Editing:** developmental editing, copyediting, and proofreading are different stages.
- **Cover design:** confirm the number of concepts and revision rounds.
- **Interior formatting:** confirm print and e-book formats, image handling, and corrections.
- **ISBN and metadata:** verify ownership and which formats receive separate ISBNs.
- **Printing:** ask whether the model is print-on-demand or an inventory print run.
- **Distribution:** ask for named platforms and countries instead of accepting “global distribution” as a complete answer.
- **Marketing:** require specific deliverables, duration, budget, and reporting.

This comparison prevents a low headline price from becoming expensive after necessary services are added.

## A realistic publishing timeline

The schedule depends on manuscript condition, book length, illustration requirements, and revision speed. Editing and author revisions often take longer than file upload or printing. Build time for proofreading after layout, checking the physical proof, correcting metadata, and approving the final cover. Rushing these checkpoints creates errors that remain visible in every printed copy.

## Final proof and launch checklist

Before approving publication, verify the title page, copyright page, ISBN, table of contents, chapter order, page numbers, image quality, margins, spine text, back-cover copy, price, author biography, and retailer description. Order or review a proof copy whenever possible.

After publication, check every retailer listing for the correct cover, description, author name, format, and price. Keep a copy of the final files and agreement. Your launch plan should identify the readers you want to reach, the channels you already control, and a small number of measurable activities rather than relying on a promise of guaranteed sales.

## Questions first-time authors should ask

1. Which services are included and which are optional?
2. How many editing and design revisions are included?
3. Who owns the copyright, ISBN, and production files?
4. Where exactly will the book be available?
5. How are royalties calculated and reported?
6. What is the expected schedule for this manuscript?
7. Can I review comparable books and speak with published authors?
8. What support continues after the book goes live?

Clear answers to these questions make it easier to compare publishers on quality, ownership, support, and total cost.

## What an ISBN identifies

An ISBN identifies a specific book edition and format. Booksellers, libraries, and distributors use it to distinguish titles and editions. It is an identifier, not a copyright registration, publishing licence, sales guarantee, or quality endorsement.

## Is an ISBN required to publish?

Requirements depend on the format and platform. An ISBN is commonly needed for commercial print distribution. KDP generally requires an ISBN for paperback and hardcover books, but has exceptions such as low-content books. Kindle eBooks do not require an ISBN. Check your intended distributor before applying, rather than treating an ISBN as a universal legal requirement.

## Applying in India

The Raja Rammohun Roy National Agency for ISBN provides ISBN allocation without an agency fee. Start with the [official Indian ISBN portal](https://isbn.gov.in/), follow the current application instructions, and provide the requested applicant, publication, and publisher details. The agency’s [ISBN FAQ](https://isbn.gov.in/Images/FAQs.pdf) explains identification and allocation.

A publishing service may charge for administrative assistance or include it in a wider package. That service fee is distinct from the agency’s ISBN allocation. Paying a service provider does not guarantee faster approval. Confirm processing requirements and status directly with the agency; there is no fixed approval timeline promised in this guide.

## Editions, formats, and the publisher imprint

Paperback and hardcover editions need different ISBNs. Where an eBook distributor requires an ISBN, use an identifier appropriate to that digital edition. A Kindle eBook can be published without one. Do not reuse an ISBN across incompatible formats or materially different editions.

Before allocation, agree who will be recorded as publisher, which imprint appears, and how the identifier will be used. A free KDP ISBN has platform restrictions and cannot simply be reused with another distributor. Read [KDP’s ISBN and imprint guidance](https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/help/topic/G201834170) before choosing between a platform-supplied identifier and your own allocation.

## ISBN and copyright are different

An ISBN helps identify a book; it does not establish copyright ownership. Copyright, permissions, publishing rights, and ISBN records are separate issues. Read the publishing agreement and the [Copyright Office handbook](https://copyright.gov.in/documents/handbook.html), and obtain advice where rights or contractual terms are unclear.

## Before publication

- Check the title, author name, format, edition, and publisher imprint against the allocation record.
- Check the identifier printed inside the book and supplied to retailers.
- Keep a copy of your allocation and final publication metadata.
- Confirm whether a new edition or format requires another ISBN.
- Check each platform’s current distribution requirements.

## Plan the rest of your publishing work

ISBN setup is one part of production. Editing, proofing, design, retailer metadata, and distribution also need attention. Read the [publishing process guide](/blog/how-to-publish-a-book-in-india-step-by-step-guide-2026) and compare [Ritera’s package services](/packages) before scheduling your launch.

This is one of the most asked questions by first-time authors.

Yes, authors do make money in India. But not the way most people assume.

Writing a book alone does not generate income.
The publishing model you choose determines how much you actually earn.

Traditional Publishing Earnings in India

In traditional publishing, the publisher handles editing, printing, and distribution. In return, the author earns a royalty percentage.

Typical Royalty Structure
5% to 10% for first-time authors
Up to 12% for established authors
Royalty calculated on MRP or net receipts
Example

If your book is priced at ₹299:

10% royalty = ₹29 per book
Sell 1,000 copies = ₹29,000 total earnings
Reality Check
Payments are delayed (often quarterly or yearly)
Limited control over pricing and marketing
No guarantee of high sales
Self-Publishing Earnings in India

Self-publishing gives you full control over your book, including pricing and distribution.

Platforms like Amazon KDP offer significantly higher royalties.

Typical Royalty Structure
35% to 70% royalty
Depends on pricing and distribution region

Same book priced at ₹299:

70% royalty = ~₹200 per book
Sell 1,000 copies = ₹2,00,000 total earnings

Same book. Same effort. Completely different income outcome.

What Actually Affects Author Income

Income is not just about publishing. It depends on multiple factors:

1. Pricing Strategy

Too high reduces sales
Too low reduces profit

2. Book Positioning

Clear niche books sell better than generic ones

3. Marketing Effort

Most books fail because they are not marketed

4. Distribution Reach

Global distribution increases earning potential

5. Consistency

Authors who publish multiple books earn more over time

The Biggest Mistake First-Time Authors Make

Most authors focus only on:

“How do I publish my book?”

Instead of:

“How will this book make money?”

Publishing is just step one.
Earning comes from strategy.

Can You Make a Full-Time Income as an Author in India?

Yes, but not instantly.

What It Requires
Multiple books
Strong niche positioning
Consistent marketing
International distribution

Most successful authors treat writing as a system, not a one-time project.

How to Increase Your Book Earnings
1. Choose the Right Publishing Model

Self-publishing gives higher margins

2. Optimize Your Book Pricing

Test and adjust pricing strategically

3. Focus on Discoverability

Metadata, keywords, and categories matter

4. Build a Launch Strategy

A good launch can define long-term sales

5. Think Beyond India

Global platforms increase earning potential significantly

Final Thoughts

The question is not:

“Do authors earn money?”

The real question is:

“Are you publishing in a way that allows you to earn?”

Because the difference between ₹29 and ₹200 per book
is not luck.

It is structure.

Build Your Publishing System the Right Way

Earning from it is strategic.

If you want clarity on publishing, pricing, and earning potential,

## Author income depends on the agreement and sales

There is no single reliable income figure for an author in India. Earnings depend on copies sold, format, price, platform rules, contractual royalty basis, costs, and taxes. A published book can also generate little or no income. A royalty percentage alone is not a profit forecast.

## Traditional publishing agreements

Check whether royalties are calculated on the cover price or net receipts, which formats and territories the agreement covers, and when statements and payments are due. Advances, discounts, returns, and subsidiary rights may affect the calculation. Do not assume one percentage is standard for all Indian publishers.

## Platform royalties are format-specific

KDP’s paperback calculation uses a rate determined by list price and marketplace, with printing costs deducted. This differs from Kindle eBook rules. For current print calculations, use [KDP’s paperback royalty guidance](https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/help/topic/G201834330) and the [printing cost and royalty calculator](https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/royalty-calculator). Do not apply an eBook percentage to a paperback or assume a percentage of the list price is the amount paid to you.

## A hypothetical calculation

Suppose an agreement pays 10% of a ₹299 list price with no other deductions in this example. The arithmetic is ₹29.90 per copy; 1,000 copies would give ₹29,900 before applicable taxes or other costs. These are illustrative assumptions, not market averages, Ritera terms, a forecast, or guaranteed sales.

If the agreement uses net receipts instead, the same headline percentage can produce a different amount. Ask for a worked example using the actual contract, format, price, marketplace, and costs before committing.

## Royalty retention is different from the retail price

Ritera’s public positioning is that authors retain 100% of the royalties paid to them. This does not mean receiving the entire book sale price. Retailer, distribution, printing, and applicable tax deductions depend on the platform and publishing agreement. Review the exact calculation, reporting schedule, and payment terms in writing.

## Calculate the full cost of publishing

Include editing, design, production, author copies, advertising, delivery, and any recurring services in your budget. Compare net proceeds after costs rather than selecting a publishing route from the headline royalty alone. See the [self-publishing cost guide](/blog/how-much-does-self-publishing-cost-in-india-complete-guide-for-first-time-authors).

## Planning income responsibly

- Use actual sales reports and the agreed royalty basis.
- Track marketing costs separately from royalties received.
- Compare print and eBook economics separately.

## Start with manuscript readiness

A publishing schedule should be agreed for the actual manuscript. Book length, editing depth, illustrations, author revisions, and approval cycles can change the work required. There is no fixed completion time that applies to every author or publishing route.

## Editing and author revisions

Ask which editing stages are included and when you must return feedback. Developmental changes may require further writing; proofreading should follow layout so the final pages are checked. Allow time for questions, revisions, and another review where necessary.

## Design and production approvals

Plan cover concepts, revision rounds, interior formatting, image permissions, and author approval of the final files. A print proof can reveal issues that are difficult to see on screen. Confirm who signs off each stage before distribution setup begins.

Agency and retailer processing times are separate from editing and design. Confirm current ISBN requirements for your format and check application status with the agency. Retailer review and listing availability can vary by format, marketplace, and corrections requested. Neither a publishing service nor this guide can guarantee agency or retailer turnaround.

Book is printed

Introduction
Writing a book is only half the journey.

The real transformation happens during editing.

Many first-time authors in India assume:
👉 “My book is already good enough”

But in reality:
👉 Editing is what makes a book readable, professional, and publish-ready

This guide explains:

What book editing services in India include

Different types of editing

Real cost breakdown

What to expect when hiring an editor

What Are Book Editing Services?
Book editing is the process of improving your manuscript before publishing.

It involves:

Fixing grammar and language

Improving clarity

Enhancing structure

Refining storytelling

Editing is not just correction—it’s refinement.

Types of Book Editing (Very Important)
Understanding this is crucial before you pay for any service.

1. Developmental Editing (Big Picture Editing)
Focuses on:

Story structure

Flow and pacing

Character development (for fiction)

Argument clarity (for non-fiction)

👉 This is the deepest level of editing

2. Copy Editing
Focuses on:

Grammar

Sentence clarity

Consistency

👉 Makes your writing clean and professional

3. Line Editing
Focuses on:

Style

Tone

Readability

👉 Improves how your writing feels

4. Proofreading (Final Step)
Focuses on:

Typos

Minor errors

Formatting issues

👉 Done just before publishing

What to Expect from Editing Services in India
A professional editing service should provide:

Clear feedback on your manuscript

Tracked changes (so you can review edits)

Suggestions for improvement

Multiple rounds (in some cases)

Good editors don’t just correct—they guide.

How Much Do Book Editing Services Cost in India?
This is the question every author asks.

💰 Typical Cost Range
₹10,000 to ₹50,000+ for full editing 

₹0.80 to ₹4 per word depending on depth 

📊 Example Cost Breakdown
Based on manuscript size:

Up to 50,000 words → ₹10,000 – ₹25,000 

50,000–100,000 words → ₹30,000 – ₹50,000 

Above 100,000 words → ₹60,000+ 

🧠 Per Word Pricing
Proofreading → ₹0.50 – ₹1 per word 

Copy editing → ₹1 – ₹3 per word 

Developmental editing → up to ₹5 per word 

👉 Key takeaway:

Editing cost depends on:

Word count

Type of editing

Editor experience

Why Editing Costs Vary So Much
Many authors get confused seeing different prices.

Here’s why:

1. Type of Editing
Proofreading is cheaper

Developmental editing is expensive

2. Manuscript Quality
Well-written books cost less to edit

Poor drafts require more work

3. Editor Experience
Freelancers → lower cost

Experienced editors → higher cost

4. Turnaround Time
Faster delivery → higher price

Cheap vs Professional Editing (Reality Check)
Low-Cost Editing
Basic corrections

Limited feedback

Faster turnaround

Professional Editing
Deep improvements

Structural clarity

Better readability

👉 Editing is not where you should cut corners.

What Happens If You Skip Editing?
Many authors try to save money by skipping editing.

This leads to:

Poor readability

Negative reviews

Low credibility

Reduced sales

👉 Editing directly impacts your book’s success

When Should You Invest in Editing?
You should invest in editing if:

You want professional quality

You want readers to stay engaged

You plan to sell your book

Even basic editing is better than none.

Can You Edit Your Book Yourself?
Yes—but with limitations.

DIY Editing Works If:
You have strong language skills

You are willing to revise multiple times

Challenges:
You miss your own mistakes

Lack of objectivity

Limited improvement

👉 External editing always improves quality

How to Choose the Right Editing Service
Before selecting a service, check:

Sample edits

Editor experience

Clear pricing

Scope of work

Ask:
👉 What exactly is included?

Red Flags to Avoid
Very low pricing (too good to be true)

No sample edits

Vague service descriptions

No communication

👉 These often lead to poor results

Where Structured Publishing Support Helps
Many authors struggle to coordinate:

Editing

Design

Publishing

This creates confusion and delays.

Some publishing platforms focus on integrating editing into a structured workflow—ensuring that your manuscript is refined as part of a complete publishing process.

For example, platforms like Ritera Publishing emphasize clarity, guided editing, and step-by-step refinement—helping authors avoid fragmented services and inconsistent quality.

A Smarter Approach to Editing
Instead of asking:

❌ “What is the cheapest editing option?”

Ask:

✅ “What level of editing does my book need?”

Because:

Not every book needs heavy editing

But every book needs some level of editing

Final Thoughts
Editing is not an expense.

It is an investment in:

Your book’s quality

Your credibility as an author

Your reader experience

The difference between an average book and a professional book is often editing.

If you’re unsure what level of editing your manuscript needs, understanding your current draft quality can help you make better decisions before publishing.

FAQs 

1. How much do book editing services cost in India?
Editing typically costs between ₹10,000 and ₹50,000 or more depending on word count and level of editing required.

2. What is included in book editing services?
It includes grammar correction, structure improvement, clarity enhancement, and sometimes rewriting suggestions.

3. Which type of editing do I need?
If your manuscript needs structural improvement, choose developmental editing. For grammar and clarity, copy editing or proofreading may be enough.

4. Is editing necessary before publishing a book?
Yes, editing significantly improves readability, quality, and credibility.

5. Can I publish a book without editing?
You can, but it may lead to poor reader experience and lower success.

6. How long does editing take?
Editing usually takes 1–3 weeks depending on manuscript size and complexity.

7. Are there publishing services that include editing?
Yes, some publishing platforms offer integrated editing as part of their workflow. For example, platforms like Ritera Publishing provide structured editing support along with publishing guidance, helping authors maintain consistency and quality.

8. What is the difference between editing and proofreading?
Editing improves content and structure, while proofreading focuses on final error correction.
